question: True or false: a striker's outstretched arm beyond the last defender can make him offside?
answer: False. For offside the hands and arms of every player, goalkeepers included, are ignored, and the law puts the top of the arm at the bottom of the armpit. A shoulder, a knee or a toe can be offside; a fingertip cannot, since a player may not legally score with it.
move: Before judging whether a line was crossed, ask which parts are allowed to count.
trap: Assuming any part of the body past the line counts.
source: IFAB, Laws of the Game, Law 11
